chief_complaint: waking up with hives and shortness of breath in the middle of the night
hpi_details: 42M presents after two episodes of waking up at 3 AM with severe generalized urticaria, abdominal cramps, and wheezing. He notes these episodes occur about 4-6 hours after eating steak or pork for dinner. He recently moved to a wooded area and reports multiple tick bites over the summer.
ideas: thinks he is developing an allergy to his new laundry detergent
concerns: terrified he might stop breathing in his sleep
expectations: wants an allergy test for environmental allergens
social_hx: Landscaper, lives in a wooded area, non-smoker

core_concepts: Alpha-gal syndrome is an IgE-mediated delayed anaphylactic reaction to galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose, a carbohydrate found in mammalian meat.
Reactions characteristically occur 3-6 hours after ingestion, often waking patients from sleep.
Sensitization is triggered by tick bites (especially the Lone Star tick in the US).
Avoidance of mammalian meat (beef, pork, lamb) is the primary management.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: waking up with hives and shortness of breath in the middle of the night
Key HPI features: Delayed (3-6 hour) anaphylaxis following red meat consumption. History of tick exposure.
Objective/Exam findings: Unremarkable between episodes. During acute episode, typical signs of anaphylaxis (urticaria, wheezing, hypotension).
common_misconceptions: Dismissing food allergy because the reaction occurs hours after the meal, rather than immediately.
Testing for standard meat proteins instead of the alpha-gal carbohydrate.
Advising avoidance of chicken or fish (which are safe).
dangerous_errors: Failing to prescribe an Epinephrine auto-injector for these potentially life-threatening episodes.
Not recognizing the delayed presentation, leading to misdiagnosis of 'idiopathic' anaphylaxis.
management_principles: Strict avoidance of mammalian meat and sometimes mammalian-derived byproducts (e.g., dairy, gelatin) if highly sensitive.
Refer to Allergy/Immunology for specific IgE testing to alpha-gal.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Symptoms may wane over years if further tick bites are avoided.

source_refs.title: World Allergy Organization (WAO) Anaphylaxis & Angioedema Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 42M presents with delayed-onset nocturnal anaphylaxis (urticaria, wheezing, GI symptoms) occurring 4-6 hours after consuming mammalian meat. Endorses recent tick bites.
reference_soap.objective: Well-appearing today. Vitals stable. Lungs clear, no rash.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Avoid all mammalian meat (beef, pork, lamb, venison). Poultry and fish are safe. 2. Prescribed Epinephrine auto-injector (0.3mg) 2-pack. 3. Refer to Allergy for alpha-gal IgE testing.

learning_objectives: Recognize the unique delayed timeline of alpha-gal anaphylaxis
Identify the association between tick bites and alpha-gal sensitization
Provide appropriate dietary avoidance counseling (mammalian meat)

teaching.one_liner: A delayed allergy to red meat, transmitted by tick bites, causing anaphylaxis several hours after eating.

must_ask.say: What did you eat for dinner in the hours before these attacks?
Have you noticed any tick bites recently?
Did you feel like your throat was closing or have trouble breathing?

history.answer: I woke up in the middle of the night with severe hives all over my body and had trouble catching my breath.
This has happened twice over the past month, both times waking me up suddenly around 3 AM. The itchy welts spread across my chest, arms, and legs within minutes.
The hives were spread widely across my chest, back, stomach, arms, and thighs. They weren't limited to one side or just on my hands and feet.
They were raised, bright red, puffy welts that coalesced into large patches. There were no blisters, scabs, or peeling skin.
The hives were intensely itchy and felt hot, but my skin wasn't painful or tender before they broke out.
The individual welts lasted several hours through the night, but by late morning or early afternoon they completely vanished without a trace.
I had two distinct episodes in the past month. I didn't take any medication during them because the symptoms eventually calmed down on their own.
Both times I woke up with bad abdominal cramping and nausea right as the hives appeared, but I didn't throw up or have diarrhea.
I was wheezing and felt like my chest was tight, making it very hard to catch my breath for about an hour. It felt like I couldn't pull enough air in.
My lips and around my eyes felt somewhat swollen and puffy, but my throat did not swell completely shut.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, body aches, or general fatigue.
No, I have no sores, blisters, or irritation inside my mouth, eyes, or genital area.
No, my skin has never peeled or blistered, and I have no dark purple spots that remain when pressed.
Both attacks happened about four to six hours after eating a heavy dinner with steak or pork chops. I felt completely fine right after the meal.
We recently switched to a new scented laundry detergent, so I wondered if that was the culprit, but I haven't handled new cosmetics, metal jewelry, or poison ivy.
I work outdoors doing landscaping and recently moved to a wooded property, so I had multiple tick bites over this past summer.
No, I was sound asleep in bed when both attacks began, not exercising or working out.
I haven't applied any steroid or antifungal creams because the rash disappears completely within several hours.
No one in my household or at my landscaping job has had any rash or similar problems.
No, I have never had asthma, eczema, hay fever, or any allergic reactions before this.
No, my joints feel normal and my fingernails have not changed at all.
I have been faithfully married to my wife for fifteen years, have had no new partners, and have never had any genital sores or infections.
I've been thinking I might have developed an allergy to the new laundry detergent my wife started using on our bedsheets.
I am terrified that my airway will swell shut and I'll suffocate in my sleep before I can wake up or call for help.
I would like to get an allergy skin test or blood work today to figure out which environmental trigger is setting this off.
I have no history of chronic medical conditions like hypertension, diabetes, or heart disease.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I don't take any prescription drugs, over-the-counter pain relievers, vitamins, or herbal remedies.
I have no known allergies to penicillin, aspirin, or any other medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any nicotine products.
I have a beer or two on the weekend, but I was not drinking heavily on the nights this happened.
I work full-time as a landscaper and live in a wooded suburban house with my wife.
Both of my parents are in their seventies and healthy, with no family history of severe allergies or autoimmune illnesses.

exam.finding: Alert, well-appearing, and in no acute distress; breathing comfortably on room air.
Blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.7 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are clear without injection, discharge, or pallor; sclerae are anicteric.
Oral mucosa is moist and intact; lips, tongue, and uvula show no swelling, erosions, or erythema.
No cervical, submandibular, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy palpated.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with vesicular breath sounds; no wheezing, rhonchi, or crackles.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops heard.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended without guarding, rigidity, or palpable masses.
Skin is warm and dry without active urticarial wheals, erythema, scaling, or purpura; palms, soles, and interdigital webs are clear.
